page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-96 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processors, the instance delivers 96 vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 192 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local storage disks, requiring external network block storage, and contains no integrated graphics processing units.

Performance metrics highlight substantial computational density across parallel and single-threaded execution. Benchmark evaluations position the instance in the top tier for multi-core stress-ng (165,189.4) and Geekbench multi-core workloads (27,814.0), alongside strong Clang software compilation and ray-tracing performance. The AMD EPYC architecture features hardware instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI, and a 32 MB L3 cache. Memory subsystems record large-block uncached read speeds of 328.35 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 154.18 GB/sec.

Hardware allocation choices prioritize raw processor throughput while limiting memory overhead and eliminating accelerator costs. Workload fitness focuses on compute-bound pipelines such as large-scale distributed compilation, continuous integration build clusters, parallel scientific modeling, batch processing, and CPU-driven web serving infrastructure.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-96 is a compute-optimized virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 9B45 x86_64 processor. The configuration provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical multithreaded cores, paired with 192 GB of system RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, routing persistent I/O exclusively through external volumes. Equipped with AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets alongside a 32 MB L3 cache, the system achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark processor evaluations, and Clang compilation benchmarks. Its memory subsystem demonstrates uncached read throughput exceeding 328 GB/sec. By offering dense compute scaling without the cost burden of unneeded memory capacity or accelerators, the instance is targeted at distributed software builds, video encoding, CPU-based batch pipelines, and parallel compute-intensive services.
